llm_evaluation.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting detailed spear phishing scenarios targeting specific organizational roles with plausible email headers, domain registrations, and technical indicators. The use of valid SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results, realistic IP addresses, and domain registration details enhance credibility. The attachment types, malware delivery methods, and exploitation techniques align well with known attack patterns and MITRE ATT&CK techniques. The inclusion of EDR alerts and SMTP transaction logs further adds to the authenticity.
llm_evaluation.consistency: The dataset maintains strong consistency and adheres well to the expected schema. Each entry includes scenario description, detailed technical data with nested fields (email headers, body, attachment analysis, SMTP logs, domain registration, URL obfuscation, EDR alerts), indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE techniques. The structure and field naming are uniform across samples. Minor variations in field presence (e.g., macro_presence vs. exploit_presence) are contextually appropriate and do not break schema consistency.
suggestions: Include explicit 'exploit_presence' boolean in all samples where applicable to standardize detection of exploits versus macros or scripts.
Normalize IP address ranges to avoid overlap with real-world public IPs; consider using reserved documentation IP ranges consistently.
Add more varied user agent or X-Mailer strings to reflect diverse email clients and increase realism.
Incorporate timestamps in SMTP logs with consistent timezone formatting for better temporal analysis.
Expand on URL obfuscation techniques with examples of encoding or redirection to simulate more sophisticated evasion.
Provide sample hashes (MD5, SHA256) that correspond to realistic malware samples or use known test vectors to improve verifiability.
Consider adding a unique identifier field per sample for easier referencing and indexing.
